findings.title: WrapString with lim=1 never wraps single-character words
findings.property: in the output, any line containing more than one word is no wider than lim when every word fits within lim
findings.expected: "a\nb" (each one-character word fits the limit on its own line)
findings.evidence: Doc: 'WrapString wraps the given string within lim width in characters'; only words longer than lim are described as pathological. The condition `wordBufLen < lim` at line 64 is false for a one-character word when lim == 1, so the break is skipped even though the word fits on a fresh line.

review.title: WrapString with lim=1 never breaks between single-character words
review.reason: The guard `wordBufLen < lim` at line 64 exists to avoid breaking a word that already can't fit. When lim==1, the first character of every word has wordBufLen==1, so the guard is always false and no break is ever emitted. As a result, "a b" stays on one line even though each word fits on its own. For lim>=2 the first character of a word always satisfies `wordBufLen < lim`, so only lim==1 is affected. The docstring only excuses overruns for words longer than the limit, and that does not apply here. This is a real off-by-one in the guard, but lim=1 is a degenerate input and the fix is trivial, so severity is low.
